headline: Nasdaq-100 posts a fourth lower close on long-end yield stress and an oil shock, while a contained overnight range keeps mean reversion intact
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,213.17 on 20 August, down 0.72% and roughly 2.8% on the week, its fourth consecutive lower close. The decline has been a grind rather than a rout: the session traded a 261-point range between 29,378.81 and 29,118.07 and closed about 95 points off the low, so retracements have remained available on every day of the drawdown. The driver is the long end of the Treasury curve. The 30-year yield closed at 5.250% and the 10-year at 4.699%, both recovering the decline that followed the Treasury's announcement that it would more than double buybacks of 10-, 20- and 30-year debt, and both sitting near the highest levels of this cycle after minutes from the last Federal Reserve meeting read more hawkish than expected. The second pressure source is energy: Brent settled 2.4% higher at $93.78 and WTI 2.3% higher at $87.83, the highest settlements since 24 July, as the United States announced a maximum economic pressure campaign against Iran while Strait of Hormuz shipping remains restricted. Crude is up roughly 6% on the week. Cross-asset internals are conflicted rather than aligned: megacaps closed with seven of eight names lower and a mean decline near 0.9%, while semiconductors were mixed to higher, and the VIX rose 7.5% to 16.01, an elevated daily move from a historically low absolute level. Current overnight evidence is stabilising. NQ futures traded at 29,331.75, up 0.11%, inside a contained 91-point band between 29,274.25 and 29,365.50 as of 00:35 UTC, with volatility futures slightly lower and crude easing modestly. There is no observed persistent directional efficiency, no repeated extension after failed retracements, and no holding near session extremes, which is why tail risk is scored low at 12% while stress remains elevated at 59%. The session ahead concentrates conditional risk in two windows: the 13:30 UTC cash open together with the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI, and the 19:00-20:00 UTC hour, when monthly expiration flow settles into the cash close alongside weekend risk reduction. CME equity index futures halt for the weekend at 21:00 UTC.

outlookSummary: The 24-hour horizon runs from the current Asian hours through a full European and US session and ends inside the weekend closure. Asian and early European hours are scored at low tail risk on the contained overnight range. Conditional risk rises through the European morning and reaches watch level for the 13:30 UTC US cash open and the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI, where two-way repricing is the base case. The highest forecast tail score falls on the 19:00-20:00 UTC hour, when monthly options expiration settles into the US cash close alongside weekend risk reduction with an unresolved US-Iran energy escalation in the background; that hour is published as the danger window. CME equity index futures halt for the weekend at 21:00 UTC, so the final three slots describe an untradable market with minimal tail risk and residual weekend gap exposure.
